Forming in the Crystal Forest near Sentenza, these replicants appear as [glittering centipedes](https://okl-scene7.insnw.net/is/image/OKL/vmf_vendor_QIX_3500644_1422481813665_597129?wid=640&hei=436). They are about 0.1m long and scurry quickly underfoot when they are not burrowing through almost any material. They prefer to stay near gems and crystals, which they use to make their nests, which are usually buried about 1m underground, though some will be close to the surface while others will be much deeper. Their nests are fractal patterns which can function as eyes, and they breed quickly although they do not live long before they break too many legs and die. They eat mostly rocks and crystals, but will supplement their diet with insects or small animals (or incapacitated/dead large ones) for energy.

#The Ice Giant

Found in the arctic and on glaciers, these replicants have developed a thick skin of snow over an ice skeleton. Their skeleton peaks through only on the bottoms of their feet, which are wide to facilitate movement over the snow, and where their mandibles are. The Ice Giants rely on thermal vision and are most active during blizzards. They are 3m tall, with a relatively small (1m) body raised on [4 longer legs which all bend towards the centre of their body](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/ZJWevfSIar8/maxresdefault.jpg). The Ice Giant has jerky but surprisingly fast movement and hunts down fauna to feast on its water. It constructs nests of ice shaped like giant ice crystals in which it lays its eggs. The nests are well-insulated and if a traveler can fend off the owners they can find shelter from the cold in one.

#The Tree Terror

These replicants are the most common, and can be recognized by their [fractally patterned nests of twigs and vines](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Argiope_bruennichi_%28wasp_spider%29_cocoon_-_eggsack,_Arnhem,_the_Netherlands.jpg). Travelers should be wary though, for by the time one recognizes the nest one is likely already inside. And telling the replicant apart from the nest is very difficult, as least before it drops on your head and drinks your blood, injecting a powerful sedative as it does so. If the victim is too large for the replicant to finish off in one meal, it will drag them to the center of the nest and build a cell around them. The victim is then kept unconscious while the replicant and its children feed on them until they are dead. Tree Terrors start off small but can grow large enough to ensnare all but the mature tree-like Saen.

#The Bright Veins

These replicants infest the hair of the plain, appearing as a [fractally patterned set of lines](http://extension.illinois.edu/soil/SoilBiology/SSSA48_LR.jpg) on the surface of the infected plant, which eventually rupture and release spores. The infection is not necessarily fatal, but the infected plant will eventually die from loss of nutrients and fluids. Other plants can be infected besides the hair, but with less efficacy.

#The Tumblepattern

These replicants grow into [balls of fractally patterned twigs](http://vignette4.wikia.nocookie.net/killzone/images/0/09/Tumbleweed.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20150127000600), which grow in the desert until mature, at which point they blow free and roll through the desert, distributing their seeds far and wide.

#The Driftnets

These replicants grow into [massive fractal nets](http://tcktcktck.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/5645778206_0671ddde08_b.jpg) which drift through the sea, ensnaring marine life and wrapping around it before digesting it. When broken, each piece continues life on its own.
